description: Population trends for CI. Test history is one test over calendar days, from the daily JUnit rollup of every E2E run; the overview is pass rate, duration and failure mix for every run; the collapsed Compare section compares a cohort of captured runs. Each panel names its population and its window. There is no single-run detail here: the run index and the run-evidence dashboards own that, and the source SHA in the rollup table links to the commit's runs on GitHub.

panels.title: What this page answers, and which population
panels.description: The population each section reads, and the window each section covers. They are never drawn on one axis.

options.content:
**Test history reads all jobs** (every E2E run, captured or not) from the daily JUnit rollup that `ci_observe_trends.py` writes to `trends.db`. Its window is the **Days** variable, not the time picker: the rollup holds one row per day, and a day only exists for runs whose GitHub artifact still existed when the rollup ran. Artifacts live 7 days.

**Overview reads all jobs** twice: overall job and run numbers come from the central Prometheus `github_actions_*` metrics, and the failure mix comes from the workflow exporter. Its window is the dashboard time range.

Test history is per **test id** over calendar days. It is not a single run: to read one run, open it from the run index (linked in the header).

A test counts as failed when its JUnit testcase holds `<failure>` or `<error>`. A skipped test is neither a pass nor a failure and is left out of both counts.

panels.title: The 7-day artifact limit, and what the first rollup covers
panels.description: Why a per-test trend starts when it starts.

options.content:
**A run's per-test result lives only in its GitHub artifact, and GitHub deletes that after 7 days.** So the rollup can only record a day while that day's runs still have artifacts. The first rollup covers the runs of the last 7 days and nothing older: history before that cannot be reconstructed, and the coverage panel above shows it as a day that was never rolled up, not as a green day.

Run `ci_observe_trends.py --days 7` daily to keep the rollup complete. Missing a day leaves a permanent hole in per-test history; the job-level numbers on the Overview section are unaffected.

A run that uploaded no artifact, an artifact larger than the download bound, and an artifact with no JUnit file all read as **no test data** for that run. They are counted in `runs_unavailable`, and they never contribute a pass.

panels.title: Compare — captured runs, selected cohort, dashboard time range

panels.title: Pick a cohort
panels.description: What a cohort is, the sample rule, and what this page can and cannot tell you.

options.content:
**Exact cohorts** group captures by the six identity fields: the resolved osac commit, the resolved harness checkout SHA, the reusable workflow file SHA, and the exact pytest suite, filter and marker. They are the only cohorts a comparison may use as a baseline. The requested osac ref is metadata only; a moving ref never keys a cohort.

**Ungrouped captures** lack at least one of the six identity fields: either the registry has no info-metric identity (`identity_source=none`), or an info identity has an empty or `unknown` field. They are **not exact** and are **not a baseline**, because the harness revision or another identity field was not captured. The table lists them separately, with the identity source and the reason, and never merges them into a cohort. `unknown` is never an identity value or a cohort key.

**The sample rule:** a comparison needs at least 2 captures in the cohort, and a stable median needs 3. The **Sample status** line under the cohort tables states where the current selection stands. When it says "No baseline", the tables below show a single run's tests, not a comparison.

**Observed time is not runner time.** Test spans include each test's setup and call time, tests run in parallel and overlap, and the total cannot be converted into runner minutes.

**Loading:** panels can take up to two minutes to load; a blank body while loading is not an empty result. The cohort tables read the capture registry. The span tables read Tempo and start only when this collapsed row expands. Each panel states its own result: a number, a verdict, or an explicit empty message.

Failed-test evidence sits at the bottom of this section; expand the section to inspect it. Click the OSAC commit value in an exact cohort row to load that cohort. You pick the cohort here. This section does not preselect a capture.

panels.title: How to read this comparison
panels.description: Cohort kinds and how to read the tables.

options.content:
### Two kinds of cohort

**Exact cohorts** compare captures that share the full resolved run identity: the resolved osac commit (`osac.ci.test_sha`), the resolved harness checkout SHA, the reusable workflow file SHA, and the exact pytest suite, filter and marker. The requested osac ref is shown as metadata only; a moving ref never keys a cohort. The registry returns these rows already grouped on the six identity fields, and only cohorts with at least 2 captures can act as a baseline.

**Ungrouped captures** lack at least one identity field: no info-metric identity (`identity_source=none`), or an info identity with an empty or `unknown` field. The registry returns them in a separate list, and this section shows that list in its own table. They are not exact, they are not a baseline, and they are never merged into an exact cohort. `unknown` is never a cohort value.

The table you click decides the selection: an exact cohort row sets all six identity variables. The sample status above the analysis tables states the resulting cohort size.

### Reading the tables

- **Tests using the most time** ranks tests by total observed test-span time in the selected cohort; its Captures column is the number of run attempts included (capture IDs carry the attempt). The Test column shows the test function; the Full test id column carries the complete pytest node id.
- **Failed tests in this cohort** lists the tests whose spans report error, with the captures they failed in. Compare it with the table above: a test high in both lists is where time and failures coincide. This is evidence, not a diagnosis: duration does not explain a failure.
- **Failed runs in this cohort** lists each failed test occurrence, with a link from the capture ID to the run investigation page.
- **Runs in this cohort** lists the captures behind every table above, from the cohort's own test spans. Session status and run duration are not joined here; the capture link opens the run investigation page, which has them.
- The sample status above the tables states the cohort size and its verdict. The failed-test tables sit at the bottom of this collapsed Compare section: empty means none were recorded, not broken.
- `all` and `none` are literal selection values, not wildcards.
- A test's rows are keyed by its pytest node id, and duplicate spans for one test in one capture are summed first, so a rerun cannot inflate the capture count.

panels.title: Query limits and data sources (capture registry + Tempo on expand)
panels.description: The caps this dashboard's queries actually hit, with the numbers observed live.

options.content:
- Cohort discovery reads `/api/ci-observe/cohorts`, not Tempo. The page runs no Tempo search at load; this Compare row is collapsed, so the span tables start only when a reader expands it.
- The registry groups exact cohorts on six identity fields: `osac.ci.test_sha`, `osac.ci.test_infra_sha`, `osac.ci.test_infra_workflow_sha`, `osac.ci.test_suite`, `osac.ci.test_filter` and `osac.ci.test_marker`. The requested osac ref is metadata, not a key.
- Captures with an incomplete identity (`identity_source=none`, or an info identity with an empty or `unknown` field) are returned in a separate ungrouped list. They are shown on their own and never merged into an exact cohort. `unknown` is never a cohort value.
- The cohort endpoint caps its response. When it truncates, it returns both the runs shown and the total in the window, so a page is never mistaken for the population.
- The span tables (tests, runs, failed tests, failed runs) read Tempo only after expansion. Each panel issues exactly one TraceQL query because this Grafana's Tempo plugin overwrites every additional target with the first.
- A live capture is not final: its spans arrive while the run is in progress, and freshly flushed blocks can be invisible to search for up to 15 minutes.
- The backend rejects time ranges longer than 168 hours (7 days). Keep the dashboard time range at or below that.
- Observed test-span time is not runner wall time. Tests run in parallel, so the totals overlap and cannot be read as saved runner minutes.

panels.title: Compare two revisions

options.content:
### Compare two revisions

`Compare base SHA` and `Compare head SHA` take two resolved osac commits (40- or 64-hex). The table below joins the daily per-test rollup for those two SHAs by `(repo, workflow, suite, test id)`. Deltas are head minus base: negative failures or duration is better.

The population is every CI job whose per-test JUnit the daily rollup stored in the window; it is not a per-capture comparison. `p50_duration_s` is the median of the daily p50 values, so a day with one run weighs the same as a day with ten. Read a delta next to the run counts: one flaky run can move it. A test present in only one revision is not paired with a zero; the endpoint lists it in `only_base` or `only_head`.
